note: Reish Lakish said: I am the atonement for Rabbi Ḥiyya and his sons. When the Torah was forgotten in the Land of Israel, Ezra came up from Babylonia and reestablished it; when it was forgotten again, Hillel the Babylonian came up and reestablished it; when it was forgotten yet again, Rabbi Ḥiyya and his sons came up and reestablished it. He then cites their ruling: Rabbi Dosa and the Rabbis agreed that the mats of Usha can become ritually impure and those of Tiberias cannot, and disagreed only about mats from other places.
why: The Gemara is asking what the word ḥotzalot means. Reish Lakish says it means plain mats, and this tribute introduces the teaching of Rabbi Ḥiyya and his sons on which that view rests.

note: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai was brought a cooked dish to taste, and Rabban Gamliel was brought two dates and a bucket of water, and each said: take them up to the sukka. But when Rabbi Tzadok was given less than an egg-bulk of food, he took it in a cloth, ate it outside the sukka, and did not say a blessing after it.
why: The previous mishna allows a snack outside the sukka, so the Gemara asks why this one tells a story that seems to contradict it; it answers that one may choose to be strict, then weighs Rabbi Tzadok's case against Rav Yosef and Abaye.
